Now, as for the statement regarding whether [the mind] has already arisen or not yet arisen, this refers to the presence or absence of mind based on internal and external conditions.
Since the presence or absence of mind has always been associated with outflows (*sāsrava*),

It is like a person who guards against fire by guarding against it in all its forms;
if one guards only against fire that has already broken out but does not guard against that which has not yet broken out,
one will inevitably be burned by the fire that has not yet manifested.
Having observed this, when the mind has not yet actually arisen, one truly guards against its arising;
as for the person who practices the contemplation of non-arising, they simply know how to observe the mind as it is currently arising, thereby preventing the mind from arising.
One does not know how to contemplate the mind before it has arisen.

Question:
How do ghosts and spirits know the three periods of time?
Answer:
As described in the *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra*, there was a ghost who entered the body of a woman.
The mantra-master asked,
"Why do you trouble others?
He replied:
"Throughout five hundred lifetimes, this woman has been my enemy, constantly taking my life;
I too have constantly taken her life—thus I know the past. If she relinquishes her enmity, I shall likewise relinquish mine."
The people of the time said to the woman, "You should abandon your resentment.
The woman replied, "I have already abandoned it.
The ghost observed her mind and saw that although she spoke with her mouth of having abandoned it, in her heart she had not.

By thus taking the woman's life, one knows the present; having known the past, present, and future of both oneself and others, one should understand accordingly that one kills the present in order to prevent future enmity.
Furthermore, those in the hells, who are of an even lower class, also know the past.
As it is said: "In the past, when I was a Brahmin king, he preached the Dharma to me; because I refused to believe and accept it, I have come to undergo this suffering."
Furthermore, one knows that by committing such offenses, one enters the hells and so forth.
